    """Normalize role-less public content into one provider-neutral message."""

structured.explanation: Checks that bytes or bytearray passed as top-level content (including the empty forms) raise TypeError 'Unsupported message content: <type>.' from normalize_content. With the defect, b"" and bytearray() return a message with no parts, and non-empty input fails with 'Unsupported media value: int.' instead. The checker rejects this file and never ran it, because it imports llm_router._internal.capabilities.content. The package re-export was rejected too. I could not run pytest either; the pass/fail behaviour comes from reading the code. As far as I can find, no public route reaches the defect: LLMRouter wraps content in a tuple first (router._messages_for_content), so _content_parts only ever sees tuples from the router, and tuples, lists or strings from session and tracing code. The project's own unit test file also imports normalize_content from this module.
